title: CapMem: A Benchmark for Caption-Based Episodic Memory in Egocentric Video
abstract: arXiv:2609.17688v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Wearable assistants require episodic memory over egocentric video, yet current vision-language models face bounded frame budgets, growing visual-token costs, and long-context retrieval failures. Under these practical constraints, we study whether textual captions can serve as reusable episodic memory. We define the Episodic Memory Video Caption QA task and introduce CapMem, a human-annotated benchmark with 75 videos totaling 33.7 hours, and 1,000 multiple-choice questions across 16 scenarios. On long videos (>20 min), full-coverage CaptionQA with 30s and 60s caption windows outperforms direct VideoQA for 10/12 and 8/12 models, respectively. On the same video subset, a matched-frame control across six Qwen models retains mean accuracy gains of 3.22 and 2.55 points, respectively. translated_title: CapMem：一个基于字幕的自我中心视频情景记忆基准
translated_abstract: 可穿戴助手需要对第一人称（自我中心）视频的情景记忆能力，然而当前的视觉语言模型面临帧数预算有限、视觉token成本不断增长以及长上下文检索失败等实际约束。在这些约束条件下，我们研究了文本字幕能否作为可复用的情景记忆。我们定义了“情景记忆视频字幕问答”任务，并推出了CapMem——一个由人工标注的基准，包含75个视频（总计33.7小时）以及涵盖16个场景的1,000道多选题。在长视频（超过20分钟）上，采用30秒和60秒字幕窗口的全覆盖CaptionQA分别在12个模型中的10个和8个上优于直接的VideoQA。在同一视频子集上，跨六个Qwen模型的匹配帧对照实验分别保留了3.22和2.55点的平均准确率提升。我们基于字幕引导的“检索与验证”框架进一步将准确率提升了最高5.3点。这些结果支持了字幕记忆在情景记忆任务中的有效性。
tldr: CapMem是一个评估基于字幕的第一人称视频情景记忆的人工标注基准，实验证明文本字幕可作为视觉语言模型可复用的情景记忆，在长视频问答中优于直接VideoQA，配合检索验证框架可将准确率提升最高5.3点。
en_tdlr: CapMem is a human-annotated benchmark for caption-based episodic memory in egocentric video, demonstrating that textual captions can serve as reusable episodic memory for vision-language models, outperforming direct VideoQA on long videos and boosting accuracy by up to 5.3 points with a retrieve-and-verify framework.
